title: Diplomats, Representatives of Int'l Organizations Visit Rehabilitation Center for Former Combatants in Tigray
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Representatives of the United Nations and ambassadors from various countries based in Ethiopia have visited a rehabilitation and reintegration center for former combatants in Tigray region.

title: Ethiopia Puts Youth At Center of Governance, Leadership - Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has placed youth empowerment and participation at the center of its governance and development agenda, with young people holding more than 50 percent of leadership positions at the federal level, Minister of Youth and Sports Aklilu Tadesse said.

title: Ethiopia Says Women's Leadership Indispensable to Africa's Economic Transformation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's Minister of Women and Social Affairs, Shawit Shanka, called on African countries to ensure women's equal participation in political leadership and economic decision-making, saying the continent cannot realize its full development potential while marginalizing half of its population.

title: Sudan Closes Ethiopian Consulate in Gedaref, Expels Diplomats in Retaliation for Assosa Closure
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's government has closed Ethiopia's consulate in the eastern city of Gedaref and expelled the diplomats working there, in a reciprocal move following Ethiopia's closure of Sudan's consulate in Assosa and the expulsion of six Sudanese diplomatic staff, further escalating tensions between the two neighboring countries amid competing accusations of backing armed groups in each other's territories.

title: FAJ, Uneca Eager to Deepen Media Engagement On Africa's Development Priorities
summary: [IFJ] Claver Gatete asserted UNECA's commitment to facilitating journalists' access to information and evidence to help amplify African perspectives. He also underscored the role journalists play in shaping the African narrative and telling the continent's story in ways that advance people-centred development. title: African Parties Gather in Addis to Discuss Governing for Growth
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Political party leaders, Heads of State, and policymakers from across the continent have gathered in Addis Ababa today, November 5, 2026, for the Second African Political Parties Summit (APPS) to deliberate on strategies for steering employment creation, inclusive development, and the structural transformation of African economies.

title: African Political Parties Summit Opens in Addis Ababa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Second African Political Parties Summit (APPS) kicked off this morning in Addis Ababa.

title: M-Pesa, Ethiopia Operations Push Safaricom Half-Year Profit to Sh58.2bn
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Safaricom's net profit rose by 35.9 percent to Sh58.2 billion in the six months to September, helped by higher M-Pesa revenue and growth in its Ethiopia business.

title: Malawian Nabbed in Ethiopia Over Cocaine Plot Bound for Malaysia
summary: [Nyasa Times] A 47-year-old Malawian man is behind bars in Ethiopia, accused of trying to smuggle cocaine from Malawi to Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia, hidden inside portraits.

title: Ethiopia's Demand for Presence in Red Sea Entirely Valid, Says Iss Regional Director, Representative to AU
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Being an important country,which plays a key role in the peace of the region, Ethiopia deserves a presence in the Red Sea, Paul-Simon Handy, Institute for Security Studies Regional Director for East Africa and Representative to the African Union said.

title: Conflict Continues in Ethiopia's Moyale As Borana Abba Geda, Somali Elder Harden Stance to 'Defend' Territory
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Clashes in Moyale and surrounding areas along the Oromia-Somali regional states border have continued in seven districts since the conflict erupted in Moyale town on October 18 following a dispute over the raising of a flag and the killing of a 13-year-old girl, with particularly heavy fighting in Areero district around the Dawa River basin, a river flowing within the Borana and Dawa zones of the Oromia and Somali regions, respectively.

title: Somaliland's Envoy Pays Courtesy Visit to Ethiopian Ambassador Teshome Shunde
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Hargeisa -- Somaliland's representative-designate to Ethiopia, Sharmarke Gelle, paid a courtesy visit to Ethiopian Ambassador Teshome Shunde at the Ethiopian mission in Somaliland as he prepared to begin his assignment in Addis Ababa, Gelle said on Wednesday.

title: Renewed Fighting in Ethiopia Forces Families to Flee Again in Tigray, Displaces Thousands in Amhara
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Renewed hostilities in northern Ethiopia have forced families who had recently returned to their homes in Tigray to flee again, while thousands of people are displaced in parts of the Amhara and Tigray regions, the United Nations has said.

title: From Regional Identity to Shared Nationhood - Reimagining Tigray's Future Within a United Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- In recent weeks, the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) and its ally, the Tigray Peace Force (TPF), have regained control of most major cities in Tigray, including the regional capital Mekelle, following the withdrawal of forces loyal to the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) faction led by Debretsion Gebremichael from key urban strongholds.

title: Ethiopia Expels Sudanese Diplomats As Regional Tensions Deepen
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff members to leave the country within 48 hours, a senior Ethiopian official told Reuters on Wednesday, further escalating tensions between the two neighbors amid competing allegations of support for armed groups and growing fears of a wider regional conflict.

title: Dakar 2026 - Ethiopian Elsabet Amare Takes Her Racing Dreams from Injibara to Dakar
summary: [Bird Story Agency] Inspired by her father and Ethiopian distance-running great Meseret Defar, 17-year-old Elsabet Amare is preparing to represent her country at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. The runner hopes her journey will encourage other young athletes from her hometown of Injibara.

title: Africa Urged to Strengthen Regional Power Integration for Energy Security
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Stronger regional electricity networks and effective power markets would enable African countries to utilize their energy resources more efficiently while improving the resilience of their electricity systems, United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) Executive Secretary Claver Gatete said today.

title: Death of Three, Injuries of 20 Kenyans Attributed to Ethiopia's Moyale Conflict
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A Kenyan woman was killed by a suspected stray bullet in the border town of Moyale on 2 November, bringing to three the reported number of Kenyans killed in conflict linked to ongoing clashes in Moyale of neighbouring Ethiopia, according to Kenyan media reports.

title: Rights Commission Confirms 48 Killed in Shirka Attacks, Raises Alarm Over Informal Armed Groups
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has confirmed that 48 people were killed in attacks in Shirka Woreda, Southeast Oromia, on 24 October, corroborating the death toll Addis Standard reported on 26 October based on eyewitness accounts and residents who attended the victims' mass funeral.

title: Ethiopian-American Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia, Faces Up to 22 Years in U.S. Prison
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Abraham Teklu Lemma, a naturalized U.S. citizen of Ethiopian descent and former U.S. government IT contractor, pleaded guilty on November 3 to conspiring to transmit highly classified national defense information to Ethiopian government officials, potentially exposing him to nearly 22 years in prison.

title: Ethiopian Authorities Suspend Independent Newspaper
summary: [HRW] Government Should Lift Ban, End Attacks on Media

title: Kenya Begins Registering Ethiopian Refugees Fleeing Moyale Clashes - Arrivals Surpass 50,000
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Kenyan authorities, in collaboration with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), have begun registering Ethiopian refugees fleeing renewed clashes in the border town of Moyale, as more than 50,000 people have reportedly crossed into Kenya since fighting intensified in late October.

title: Sudan Lodges Formal Complaints Against Ethiopia With UNSC, AU Peace and Security Council
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's army-aligned government has lodged formal complaints against Ethiopia with the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the African Union Peace and Security Council (AUPSC), accusing the country of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to use Ethiopian territory to launch drone attacks against Sudan.

title: Ethiopia, China Pledge to Deepen Military and Strategic Cooperation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and China have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening their longstanding military and strategic partnership.

title: Ethiopia's Governance Trajectory Shows 'Warning Signs' Despite Modest Gains: Ibrahim Index
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's overall governance performance improved modestly over the past decade, but worsening security, rule of law and rights indicators have placed the country on a trajectory marked by "Warning Signs," according to the 2026 Ibrahim Index of African Governance (IIAG).

title: Long After Ethiopia Completes GERD, Egypt, Sudan Invoke Nile Water Rights Under Colonial-Era Agreement
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Egypt and Sudan have renewed their opposition to Ethiopia's independent management of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), invoking historical Nile water-sharing agreements and demanding a binding legal framework, more than a year after Ethiopia officially inaugurated the project.

title: Will Renewed Conflict Derail Ethiopia's Economic Growth?
summary: [DW] Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. But renewed fighting in the north of the BRICS member state could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living.

title: Violence in the North Is Pushing Health System to the Brink, WHO Chief Warns
summary: [UN News] The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.
